sources.title: MythoMax-L2-13b original model card
sources.evidence: Author identifies MythoMax as a tensor merge of MythoLogic-L2 and Huginn, intended for roleplay and storywriting, with Alpaca prompts. The card labels the license other and distinguishes external quantizations. Fresh October 27 read of the exact pinned README confirms that every one of the 363 tensors is blended at an individual ratio and directly links the author’s merge script and templates; it supplies no separate active figure.

sources.title: Exact original MythoMax configuration
sources.evidence: LlamaForCausalLM: 40 layers, hidden size 5120, intermediate size 13824, 40 attention and KV heads, vocabulary 32000, untied word embeddings, FP16, maximum positions 4096 and no RoPE scaling. The August 10 upload has identical structural settings. Freshly reopened October 27; structural dimensions agree with the named MythoLogic-L2 parent.

sources.title: Original FP16 checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Indexes 363 learned weight tensors across 13 original PyTorch shards; total_size is 26,031,728,640 bytes. Includes separate embedding and output-head weights; no rotary-frequency, quantization-scale or other buffer entries. Fresh October 27 metadata read reconfirmed the 363-entry index and unchanged total_size; no shards or tensor census were retrieved in this pass.

sources.title: Original PyTorch shard metadata
sources.evidence: At revision 58e77dd48a65176f97f6f376c93efe9caad9c130, bounded HTTP range reads of ZIP directories and data.pkl metadata for all 13 original shards obtained 363 FP16 tensor shapes totaling 13,015,864,320 elements and the same unique-storage total. Only 73,070 metadata bytes were read; no tensor payloads. Shape reconstruction used inert allowlisted metadata stubs, without PyTorch or checkpoint code execution.

sources.title: Original repository commit history
sources.evidence: Initial repository commit is August 10, 2023 at 20:35:34 UTC; commit 319d19bb39fa283102032517cf89d914acff6bcf uploaded 20 model files at 20:51:49 UTC, followed by the public model card at 20:52:23. Later changes are card/config updates.

sources.title: MythoLogic-L2 original component card
sources.evidence: Identifies the component as a Llama 2 merge of Nous-Hermes-Llama2-13b, chronos-13b-v2 and airoboros-l2-13b-gpt4-2.0. Freshly read the full raw card October 27; explicitly describes the Llama 2 gradient merge and its 40-layer structure.

sources.title: Chronos-13b-v2 original component card
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies this component as an FP16 PyTorch/HF model based on LLaMA v2 Base; labels its license llama2. Fresh October 27 original-card read confirms the named LLaMA v2 Base relationship.

sources.title: Llama 2 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Base license governs Llama materials and derivative works, requiring agreement redistribution, attribution and acceptable-use compliance; it restricts improving other LLMs and includes a separate-license threshold above 700 million monthly active users.

sources.title: Gryphe response on MythoMax licensing
sources.evidence: On August 18, 2023, Gryphe permits commercial use only conditionally on all underlying models permitting it; the response does not supply an independent unconditional license.

sources.title: Llama 2 technical report
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and A.7 describe an autoregressive Transformer with RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE, text input/output, and a 4K context for 13B. Table 1 uses nominal 13B and no grouped-query attention for that size. Exact derivative configuration and tensors establish structural inheritance. Freshly reopened October 27; its nominal total is retained as supporting lineage evidence, not independently relabeled as active.

sources.title: Airoboros L2 component card and license discussion
sources.evidence: The component is Llama-2 based and explicitly requires compliance with Meta terms while leaving additional licensing ambiguous. Function/argument-generation examples concern this component, not a verified capability of the final MythoMax merge.

sources.title: Linked Huginn component card
sources.evidence: The original card links this component; its page returned HTTP 401 during this audit, so its present license and detailed lineage could not be checked. The fresh October 27 attempt again returned HTTP 401. Active-size inference instead follows the accessible MythoLogic model1 architecture and the author’s exact merge recipe; Huginn’s undisclosed details are not silently asserted.

sources.title: OpenRouter provider listing, used only to record conflicts
sources.evidence: Lists July 2, 2023 and 8192 tokens. These conflict with the original August 10 checkpoint history and its 4096-position configuration; provider-specific context and catalog dates are not transferred to the original checkpoint.

sources.title: Mixtral of Experts, original benchmark comparison
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27. Section 2.1 defines active parameter count as parameters used to process a token; Section 3 says the authors rerun the comparison models themselves. Table 2 explicitly identifies LLaMA 2 13B with 13B Active Params. This is Mistral’s original nominal comparison convention, not a Meta or Gryphe tensor-level activity disclosure.

sources.title: Author’s exact MythoMax tensor-merge recipe
sources.evidence: Freshly inspected pinned recipe linked by the original model card. Despite the filename, output_model_path explicitly ends mythomax-L2-13b; model_path1 is mythologic-L2-13b and model_path2 is The-Face-Of-Goonery_Huginn-13b-FP16. Operations blend the existing LM head, embeddings, attention, MLP and normalization tensors rather than concatenate models or add experts.

sources.title: Author’s tensor-merge implementation
sources.evidence: Freshly read source without executing it. The implementation iterates model1 state-dictionary keys, forms weighted sums with model2 tensors, loads the result back into model1 and saves model1. Vocabulary blending explicitly retains model1 dimensions. No new layers, expert expansion, structural pruning or inference router are introduced. This directly supports architecture preservation for the named MythoLogic parent of the exact recipe.

sources.title: Author’s merge-method documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27. Describes blending two fine-tuned Llama models into one model, with tensor ratios and model1 vocabulary preservation. It warns against mixing Llama 1 and Llama 2; the exact MythoMax recipe and original MythoLogic card identify the L2 lineage independently.

sources.title: Named MythoLogic L2 parent configuration
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27. LlamaForCausalLM with 40 layers, hidden5120, intermediate13824, 40 attention/KV heads, vocabulary32000 and untied embeddings matches the exact MythoMax dimensions. Combined with explicit parent and merge code, this confirms no dimensional change; similarity alone is not the lineage evidence.

sources.title: Original Nous Hermes Llama 2 component card
sources.evidence: Fresh full original raw-card read October 27. Identifies the Llama2-13B instruction fine-tune. Its distillation tag refers to training on synthetic GPT-4 outputs, not a pruned or structurally reduced student. Supports the explicitly named MythoLogic component lineage; it does not itself publish active parameters.

name.note: Readable spelling of the exact original MythoMax-L2-13b repository identifier.

developer.note: Gryphe authored the derivative merge and original upload; Meta developed its base architecture.

family.note: The documented merge lineage and exact Llama configuration establish the Llama 2 family.

release_date.note: Earliest evidenced original weight upload, 20:51:49 UTC. Provider listings and later quantization uploads do not establish an earlier original release.

open_weights.note: All 13 original FP16 shards and their metadata are publicly accessible; this does not imply an unrestricted open-source license.

license.value: other; inherited Llama 2 Community License restrictions
license.note: Author metadata says other. Llama 2 ancestry entails Meta restrictions; Gryphe makes commercial use conditional on underlying permissions. This descriptive classification does not resolve the full merge license: Airoboros leaves terms ambiguous and Huginn was inaccessible.

parameters_b.note: Complete unique learned checkpoint count: 13,015,864,320 = 2*32000*5120 + 40*(4*5120^2 + 3*5120*13824 + 2*5120) + 5120. Untied embedding and head each contribute 163,840,000. All 363 FP16 shapes and unique storage totals agree with index bytes/2; no quantization tensors or buffers included. 13B is nominal. October 27 re-audit retains this supported exact total and reconfirms the original nominal 13B size through developer-named merge lineage. Pinned card/config/index and author merge source were freshly checked; no weight shards or repeat tensor census were needed.

active_parameters_b.note: Inferred nominal 13B active under Mistral’s published Llama 2 13B comparison convention in Mixtral Table 2. The original MythoMax card and exact author recipe explicitly merge MythoLogic-L2 with Huginn; the implementation preserves model1’s structure and vocabulary, and the original MythoLogic card traces that model to named Llama 2 13B fine-tunes. Fresh exact configurations confirm unchanged dimensions, with no added experts, pruning or new modalities. Huginn remains inaccessible, but the explicit model1-preserving recipe establishes the relevant parameter structure without assuming its private details. This is attributed nominal lineage inference, not a direct Gryphe active-count disclosure or a claim that all 13.01586432B checkpoint elements participate per token. Fresh exact-model total, active and activated searches found no more precise original count; secondary dense-equals-total assertions are not the basis.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Llama Transformer: 40 blocks, standard 40-head attention, SwiGLU MLPs, RMSNorm and RoPE. Complete tensor inventory contains no experts or router; embedding and LM head are untied.

context_window.note: Original and current author configurations specify 4096 positions with rope_scaling null. The provider-listed 8192 is not an original-checkpoint context claim.

modalities.note: Text tokenizer embeddings and causal vocabulary head match the author prompt format; no multimodal encoder or projector exists in the complete checkpoint.

reasoning.note: No exact-model reasoning-mode specification establishes either Boolean value. Generic reasoning evaluations of components or base models do not verify this field; clear baseline false.

tool_call.note: No exact-model tool-call protocol is documented. Airoboros component function examples do not prove support survives this tensor merge, and a serving endpoint restriction is not a checkpoint-wide claim; clear baseline false.

description.value: Llama 2 merge combining MythoLogic and Huginn for creative writing and roleplay
description.note: The original author documents the named merge and intended writing uses; this description makes no comparative performance claim.

patch.license: other; inherited Llama 2 Community License restrictions
patch.notes: Original Gryphe FP16 checkpoint contains 13,015,864,320 unique learned parameters, including untied input/output embeddings. Nominal active 13B follows Mistral’s Llama 2 comparison convention through the documented MythoLogic tensor-merge lineage; it is not a separate Gryphe measurement. The merge preserves the parent architecture. License metadata is other, with inherited Llama 2 restrictions and unresolved component terms; commercial permission is conditional. Original release is 2023-08-10 with 4096 context, despite conflicting provider listings. Reasoning mode and tool calling remain unverified.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the exact 13.01586432B total and recovers nominal active 13B through explicit Llama 2 merge lineage and Mistral’s original active-parameter comparison. Fresh author card, pinned config/index, exact merge YAML and implementation establish architecture preservation without a repeat tensor census. Huginn’s card remains inaccessible and its details are not asserted. All nonparameter assessments and prior corrections are preserved.
